label: z as the 3rd original token, gated by which tokens come before it
explanation: Fires almost only when the input at step t=2 (the third original token) is z: that covers 99.5% of activations and 99.9% of mass, but only about 11% of t=2 z steps fire. It never fires on z at any other position, on other tokens, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (1 stray copy-phase activation). Whether it fires and how strongly depends on the two tokens before it. It is strongest when the first token is i (top examples are i z z, at max) or r (r z z, 0.83 of max), then l, j and g. It also fires when the second token is z or g. A first-token/second-token conjunction raises precision to 0.79 but lowers mass recall. The simple rule (t=2, z, and first token in {i,r,l,j,g} or second token in {z,g}) gives dev precision 0.48, recall 0.89, mass recall 0.97. The exact prefix dependence looks like a lookup over (tok0, tok1) pairs and is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 39 cues. Raise it: t=2 & in_tok=z (+5.28), orig0=i (+2.41), t=2 & prev_tok=s (+2.37), prev2_tok=r (+2.13), t=2 & prev_tok=g (+2.10), t=2 & prev_tok=z (+2.05). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.26), in_first=1 (-2.02), orig0=t (-1.25), prev_tok=i (-1.23).
